thread:
sophia: Quick sync: sizing for new 30B dedicated pools. Need H100 vs A100 numbers across us-east1/eu-west1. Targets: p50 < 80ms, p99 < 600ms for short-chat. What's realistic per-GPU concurrency and autoscale headroom?

liam: Ran microbench today with 30B q4f16 and kernel optimizations. Short summary:
```
region,gpu,concurrency,p50_ms,p99_ms,tokens_per_s_per_gpu
us-east1,H100,64,42,480,220
us-east1,A100,64,55,720,150
eu-west1,H100,64,48,510,210
eu-west1,A100,64,60,740,140
```
These were batch=1 steady-state with prefix caching disabled (worst-case). p99s on A100 are consistently above our target at 64c.

marta: Hmm. For SLA we can't let p99 exceed 600. Options: reduce target concurrency on A100, use H100, or increase pooled GPUs + lower per-GPU concurrency.

raj: My rough rule: steady per-GPU concurrency = tokens_per_s_target / tokens_per_s_per_gpu. For typical short chat (avg 8 tok/s per request) and 200 rps target per pool, that maps to ~1600 tok/s -> you'd need 8 H100 (8*220=1760) or 11 A100 (11*150=1650). Add headroom.

owen: Cost note — H100 instance ~$X/hr (committed), A100 cheaper per-hour but needs ~30% more GPUs. For mid-sized customer, H100 ends up ~10-15% cheaper total due to fewer GPUs and lower networking tail.

marta: Headroom — proposed autoscale policy:
```
steady_target_concurrency_per_gpu:
  H100: 70
  A100: 40
autoscale_headroom_multiplier: 1.25
burst_pool_multiplier: 1.5
reserve_pool: 10% of steady
```
This keeps p99 under 600 and gives room for short spikes.

liam: Agree. Also suggest kernel fallback: prefer fused-gemm kernels on H100; on A100 fall back to tiled kernels for long sequences. That reduces p99 variance.

devops-bot: autoscale changes staged in canary: /policies/dedicated/30b-headroom-v2 applied to us-east1-canary

sophia: Plan: liam attach raw bench logs + perf flamegraphs. marta update pricing calc + rollout RFC. I'll draft cross-region fallback runbook (if eu-west H100 is saturated, spill to us-east with region routing). Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
